extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals submitting Silver Anvil Strategic Campaign entries (PRSA entrants and members)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and packaging a Silver Anvil Strategic Campaign award submission, including the required two-page summary, supporting materials, visuals, and formatting so judges can evaluate campaign strategy, execution, and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-page summary quality and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: A two-page summary of the campaign, with supporting materials, is required for each submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary must be typed and use no smaller than a 10-point typeface and one-inch margins. The summary is the best way to concisely make the case for a campaign’s excellence and PRSA says the two-page summary is the most consequential element upon which judges make their decisions. Don’t treat the summary as an afterthought; take time to write it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting materials: insights, analysis, planning, execution, evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should include supporting materials that cover the campaign’s insights and analysis, planning, execution and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges may read extensive supporting materials (in some cases 50 or more pages; PRSA notes supporting materials can run as long as 225 pages), so include substantive documentation of strategy, tactics, and how outcomes were measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual appeal and use of graphics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing many entries in a row, judges can be overwhelmed by page after page of text. Colorful charts and beautiful imagery make an entry stand out — but visuals should help tell a compelling story of success. Each Silver Anvil Strategic Campaign entry can include up to three graphic images representative of the campaign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar and proofreading
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grammatical errors shouldn’t automatically disqualify a strong entry, but missing or misplaced punctuation may influence some judges. An extra set of proofreading eyes is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance, timeliness and passion
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaigns that address timely issues and show passion and energy are notable to judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions informed by current events or social needs (examples given: voter turnout efforts, COVID-19 information to diverse communities, 2020 census outreach) stood out; judges saw ambition in efforts supporting timely causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear demonstration of success and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must tell a compelling story of success supported by evidence and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the summary and supporting materials to show outcomes and how the campaign met objectives. 'Compelling story of success' should be evidenced through metrics, analysis and documented evaluation rather than unsupported claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and readability to aid judge review
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the case concisely so judges do not get lost in voluminous data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because supporting materials can be extensive and judges may review many entries, the two-page summary and organized materials should distill the most important points so evaluators can quickly grasp strategy, impact, and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to small elements and details
rubrics_metrics.description: Seemingly small elements within entries can make a big difference in close decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful presentation, completeness, clarity, and other small details (formatting, organization, clear visuals, error-free writing) can tip judges toward or against an entry in a tightly contested category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to submission limits and instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow stated submission rules and limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with required summary length/format, allowed number of graphic images (up to three), and any other instructions; failure to follow formatting or submission instructions can undermine judges' ability to evaluate an entry effectively.
